headlines: {A.last} Siblings Split a Quilt, Keep the Peace
Old Quilt Finds Room for Two
Family Keepsake Becomes Two Smaller Keepsakes
bodies: {A} and {B} settled a dispute over an old family quilt by dividing it into two lap blankets. Each insisted the other take the warmer half.
An argument over a family quilt ended when {A} suggested making two smaller blankets. {B} agreed, and the pair left together carrying matching bundles.
{A} and {B} brought scissors to a family disagreement and managed a peaceful ending. Their shared quilt is now two blankets, with the original border divided evenly.

headlines: Family Quilt Dispute Unravels in Public
One Quilt, Two Claims, No Agreement
Keepsake Argument Leaves a Family Divided
bodies: {A} refused to share an old family quilt with {B}. Their argument spilled onto {street}, where neither found a sympathetic audience.
A disagreement over a family quilt brought {A} and {B} into a public quarrel. {A} kept the blanket, while {B} left empty-handed.
{A} carried away a disputed family quilt despite objections from {B}. Several witnesses suggested that keeping warm might now be easier than keeping company.

items.era_notes: Quilts and hand sewing work in every decade; do not imply either sibling has lost a parent.

headlines: Ducklings Leave Drain, Crowd Finally Leaves
bodies: {A} and {B} coaxed trapped ducklings from a roadside drain using a board and a trail of crumbs. The birds returned to the river without acknowledging the applause.
A roadside gathering watched {A} lower a board into a drain while {B} scattered crumbs above it. Every trapped duckling climbed out, and the two rescuers shook hands.
Traffic paused on {street} while {A} and {B} freed ducklings from a drain. The rescue required one borrowed board and considerably more patience than either expected.

headlines: Ducklings Escape; Rescuer Loses a Good Coat
Drain Rescue Costs a Coat, Gains a Friend
Small Birds Depart Before Help Arrives
bodies: {A} tore a coat reaching into a drain for trapped ducklings, which promptly escaped through another opening. {B} helped with the climb back out and offered a sympathetic walk home.
The ducklings in a roadside drain found their own exit while {A} was attempting a rescue. {B} helped {A} out, though a badly torn coat proved beyond saving.
A duckling rescue on {street} ended with the birds safe and a coat ruined. {B} stayed to help {A}, and the pair departed laughing at the ungrateful beneficiaries.

items.era_notes: Use foot traffic or generic traffic; avoid emergency services or technology assumptions.

items.text: They say {A} practices speeches for a public office after closing {shop}.
variants: I hear {A} rehearses speeches at {shop}; it takes nerve to offer yourself up for everybody's complaints.
Word is {A} wants public office and practices at {shop}.
If {A} is only talking to the mirrors at {shop}, why do people say there are campaign speeches involved?

items.text: I hear {A} has been returning lost mittens to the school steps in pairs that do not match.
variants: They say {A} is getting lost mittens back to school; two warm hands matter more than matching colors.
{A} supposedly returns the mittens, mismatched and all.
Who told {A} which mittens belong together, or is this supposedly a whole new system?

items.text: Word is {A} copied a private letter from {B} and read it aloud for laughs.
variants: I hope that story about {A} reading a letter from {B} is wrong; trust is hard to mend.
They say {A} made entertainment out of a private letter from {B}.
What was in that letter from {B} that {A} supposedly thought everybody needed to hear?

items.text: People say {A} refuses firewood unless someone calls it payment for sharpening a pencil.
variants: They say {A} will trade pencil sharpening for firewood; everybody needs a way to keep their pride warm.
Apparently {A} takes wood for sharpening pencils and calls it square.
How sharp must a pencil be if people say {A} earns a whole armload of wood for it?

items.text: They say {A} found a folded map inside a hollow fence post, with every road ending at the church.
variants: I hear {A} found a strange map in a fence post; perhaps somebody just drew the routes they knew.
{A} supposedly found a map where every road ends at the church.
Why hide a map in a fence post, and why do people say {A} will not show anyone the other side?

items.text: I hear {A} waters down the soup at {shop} whenever the lunch crowd looks bigger than expected.
variants: They say {A} stretches the soup at {shop}; I hope it is worry about feeding everyone, though customers deserve to know.
Crowded room, thinner soup at {shop}; that is the word about {A}.
Has anybody watched the soup pot at {shop} when more customers arrive? People say {A} reaches straight for the water.
